title: Jude and the Parish
premise: Ivo Villalobos, a reclusive estate lawyer who has spent decades drafting other people's endings, is summoned to the parish of St. Aldhelm's to execute a will naming them as sole executor—a will for a woman, Edith Marsh, who Ivo slowly realizes was their own mother, given up at birth and living under a borrowed name. Among her papers is a parish ledger whose entries are a coded confession to a decades-old death, plus an anonymous letter postmarked the day after her funeral claiming the confession is false. As the statute of limitations closes in, Ivo decodes the ledger with help from the parish's ragtag found family—the verger, the organist, a runaway teen—and discovers Edith took the blame for a fire that killed the old vicar, shielding the true culprit: her lifelong friend, the current churchwarden. In the end, Ivo chooses truth over inheritance, exposing the confession's falsity just before the deadline, and claims not the estate but the family that gathers around it.
about_author: Vesper Coldharbour is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent eleven years reading other people's final wishes before starting to invent her own. She writes mysteries about paperwork, small towns, and the families we assemble rather than inherit.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ivo Villalobos receives a certified letter summoning them to St. Aldhelm's parish to execute the will of one Edith Marsh—whose name matches documents from Ivo's own sealed adoption file. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into compulsion; the invisible life begins to crack.

chapters.title: Postmarked the Day After
chapters.summary: At the funeral, Ivo observes the mourners—an organist who weeps theatrically, a churchwarden named Harold Finch who watches Ivo too closely. That evening an anonymous letter arrives claiming Edith's enclosed confession is a lie. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger who wasn't a stranger.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Borrowed Life
chapters.summary: Ivo catalogs Edith's cottage per the will: hymnals with marginalia, photographs of a child Ivo recognizes as themselves, and a leather parish ledger with numbers where names should be. The runaway teen squatting in the garden shed, Wren, refuses to leave. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: tenderness arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: The Verger Knows Everything
chapters.summary: Dennis Okafor, the verger, lets slip that Edith visited the ledger room every Thursday for forty years. He also mentions the 1984 vestry fire that killed Vicar Ambrose Thorne—ruled accidental, closed quickly. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: first solid thread; curiosity becomes investigation.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Ivo realizes the ledger's columns are a book cipher keyed to the parish register of births. Entries cluster around dates Ivo doesn't recognize—until one resolves into words: 'I did it. God forgive me.' POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: dread; the confession is real, dated three days after the fire.

chapters.title: Wren's Terms
chapters.summary: Wren bargains: food and a locked door in exchange for silence about Ivo's midnight research. Their wary negotiation reveals Wren fled a group home and Edith had been secretly feeding them for months. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: two guarded people discovering mutual usefulness.

chapters.title: The Organist's Requiem
chapters.summary: Organist Marguerite Pell plays a requiem 'for Edith' that isn't on any service list; its structure mirrors the ledger's column pattern. She admits Edith taught it to her but begs Ivo to stop digging: 'Some confessions keep people safe.' POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: warning wrapped in mourning.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Ivo consults their old mentor by phone: if the fire was arson, prosecution expires in weeks; but proving the confession false voids a codicil leaving the cottage to the parish—which Finch is eager to sell. Money, they realize, is a motive. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the mystery acquires stakes beyond the past.

chapters.title: Harold Finch's Generosity
chapters.summary: Finch hosts Ivo for tea, charming and precise, offering to 'handle' the estate paperwork himself. He mentions the fire unprompted, with details only a witness would know. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: charm curdling into suspicion; the reader sees what Ivo half-sees.

chapters.title: What the Register Hides
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing the cipher, Ivo finds a page torn from the birth register—dated nine months before Ivo's birth. Edith Marsh gave up a baby in 1978. The realization lands physically. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: vertigo; the case is personal now.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Edith's hymnal notes, decoded against the ledger, form letters to the child she lost—apologies, descriptions of Sundays, a repeated phrase: 'I carry someone else's sin so you won't have to.' POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the confession reframes as sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Fire, Retold
chapters.summary: Dennis produces a boxed newspaper archive. The 1984 coverage names Edith as the one who raised the alarm—but a photo shows young Harold Finch's car parked behind the vestry at 2 a.m., hours before the 'morning' blaze. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the shape of the truth emerges.

chapters.title: Wren Runs
chapters.summary: A social worker traces Wren to the cottage; panicking, Wren flees with a ledger page as collateral, convinced Ivo will hand them over. Ivo searches the freezing streets all night. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: fear of belonging; found family tested at its weakest joint.

chapters.title: Found in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Ivo finds Wren in the tower at dawn. Instead of calling anyone, Ivo offers them the executor's spare key and a place at the table. Wren returns the page. POV: alternating Ivo/Wren. Emotional beat: the book's quiet center—belonging chosen, not granted.

chapters.title: Finch Makes His Move
chapters.summary: Finch files to contest the will, citing Ivo's 'undisclosed relation' to the deceased, and petitions to expedite the cottage sale. He also reports Wren's presence to authorities. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: siege; the antagonist weaponizes procedure.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Another anonymous letter arrives—same postmark trick, different handwriting analysis: it quotes a line from Edith's marginalia never made public. Whoever writes knows the cottage intimately. Suspicion shifts toward Marguerite. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: paranoia; allies become suspects.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Organ
chapters.summary: Ivo corners Marguerite after evensong. She breaks: Edith confessed everything to her years ago—not guilt, but protection. 'She said Harold lit it, and that his family owned half the parish. Who would believe her?' POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: testimony; the coded ledger finally makes sense.

chapters.title: Decoding the Last Entry
chapters.summary: With Wren's fresh eyes and Dennis's register access, Ivo cracks the final cipher entry: coordinates to a tin box in the churchyard wall containing Finch's signed insurance claim, filed before the fire was even reported. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by grief—Edith died carrying proof no one read.

chapters.title: The Deadline
chapters.summary: Two days before the statute expires, Ivo delivers the evidence to a detective who once owed their mentor a favor. Finch is questioned; he doesn't deny it—he asks only whether Edith suffered. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: cold justice; victory without satisfaction.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: The fraudulent codicil voided, the cottage passes to Ivo—who declines to sell, instead granting Wren tenancy and Dennis the archive. At the hearing, Ivo states their relationship to the deceased aloud for the first time: 'She was my mother.' POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: claiming identity out loud.

chapters.title: Thursdays at St. Aldhelm's
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Ivo takes up Edith's ritual: Thursdays in the ledger room, now joined by Wren doing homework, Dennis with tea, Marguerite rehearsing. The anonymous letters are traced to Edith herself—scheduled before her death, mailed by a solicitor's standing instruction. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: revelation softened into gift; even the mystery was a hand reaching out.

chapters.title: The Parish Register
chapters.summary: Ivo adds a new line to the restored birth register—not erasing the past but continuing it: their own name beside Edith's, and beneath it, Wren's, entered as household. Closing image: candles in the vestry window where the fire began. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: resolution; memory kept, belonging written down.
